content: BBC’s Blue Planet III is looking to prove its authenticity by leaving in the less-than-perfect shots. Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real. But one dead giveaway of AI is when things look too polished and seamless. To counter that, Blue Planet III goes warts and all. Executive Producer Elizabeth White told The Guardian in the past, “the amount of plankton and things” floating in the water would have caused them to cut a shot. Or “we might have framed out a boat or a buoy or gone: ‘Oh, actually … the water conditions are not really good enough for this.’” Instead, this time they’re leaving it all in to show a more authentic, organic version of the oceans. The series features incredible displays of dolphins trapping fish by plugging holes with sea sponges, inter-species fish communication, and 200,000 crabs lining up in formation to feed. White says that real ocean creatures “are probably more remarkable than AI could imagine.”

chineseContent: BBC 的《蓝色星球 III》希望通过保留不太完美的镜头来证明其真实性。之前的自然系列作品以绚丽、晶莹剔透的镜头为特色，看起来好得令人难以置信。但人工智能的一个致命弱点是，事情看起来过于完美和无缝。为了解决这个问题，《蓝色星球 3》就彻底失败了。执行制片人伊丽莎白·怀特（Elizabeth White）过去告诉《卫报》，漂浮在水中的“浮游生物和其他东西的数量”会让他们放弃拍摄。或者“我们可能会画出一艘船或一个浮标，或者离开：‘哦，实际上......水的条件对于这个来说还不够好。’”相反，这一次他们把一切都留在了里面，以展示更真实、有机的海洋版本。该系列节目展示了令人难以置信的海豚用海绵堵住洞来捕获鱼类、物种间鱼类交流以及 200,000 只螃蟹排成队形捕食的场面。怀特说，真正的海洋生物“可能比人工智能想象的更引人注目”。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
